resources.string: Enable listening to record and adjust reminder times with the screen locked or off. One gesture is two firm back-and-forth movements. With the default assignments, one gesture starts recording and another stops it. Shake again shortly after stopping to edit the time. Recordings stop after 5 minutes.

Sounds follow your notification volume and silent-mode settings. Listening uses battery and shows an ongoing notification. Enable it again after restarting the phone or if Android stops the app. Some phones need unrestricted battery access for reliable screen-off detection.
Use your configured start gesture to record. Tap for controls and gesture assignments.
Use your configured stop gesture, or Stop and save. You can then adjust the reminder time by shaking.
Reminder scheduled. Open it to preview the recording or change its time. The action log shows its due time.
Reminder scheduled, but the microphone reported very little sound. Open the reminder to preview it.
Recording saved, but the reminder could not be created. Open the recording below to try again.
Reminder saved, but its alarm could not be scheduled. Open the reminder and save its time again.
Could not capture a complete recording. Check microphone access and free storage, then try again.
Could not enable listening. Open SpeakAlert, allow microphone and notifications, then try again.
This device does not have an available accelerometer.
Microphone and notification access are needed so you can record and stop listening from the lock screen. If permission was denied, allow it in Android app settings.
New shake recordings become reminders automatically. Older recordings and any that could not become reminders appear here for recovery.
This recording has not been attached to a reminder. Deleting it cannot be undone.
This recording could not be opened. It may have been deleted or storage may be full.

Assign single, double and triple gestures separately for each mode. A gesture is two firm movements; repeat the full gesture to make a double or triple. Wait for the grouping pause to finish before the action runs. Four or more gestures in one group are ignored. During time editing, the short cue means Minutes mode and the double cue means Hours mode.
Stop listening before saving new settings. Your current recording or time edit will be saved first.
Time to enter editing after recording (seconds)
1–1440 minutes. Hours mode can use any increment, including 30 minutes.
3–60 seconds. Pausing automatically saves the selected time.
600–2500 ms. Must be at least 400 ms longer than the minimum pause. A longer grouping pause makes doubles and triples easier but delays each action.
200–1200 ms. Short pauses make repeated gestures easier; longer pauses reduce accidental repeats.
1.8–4.5 g. Lower values need less force and may trigger accidentally.
Check the number ranges and grouping pause before saving.
Settings could not be saved. Try again.
Recording saved. Finish now or wait to schedule the reminder automatically.
Recording saved, but very little sound was detected. Preview the reminder after it is scheduled.
Due: %1$s. Use your edit gesture within %2$d seconds, or wait to keep this time.
%1$s: %2$d minutes per step. Due: %3$s. Finish with your assigned gesture or pause for %4$d seconds to save.
The last 30 recognized groups and saves from this app session. Use this to check your assignments and sensitivity. No audio is included.
Editing window ended; scheduling the selected time.
More than three gestures in one group; no action taken.
Silent updates about recording, gesture recognition, time-edit mode and reminder scheduling.
Recognizing %1$d gesture(s)… Pause to run the assigned action.
No action assigned to this gesture.
Due: %1$s. Tap to view the reminder. Listening for your next recording gesture.
Very little sound was detected; preview the recording.
